learn.title: Text is an array
learn.body: C has no separate string type. A string is an array of `char` that ends with a special byte, `'\0'`, called the null terminator. Every piece of text you print is stored this way.

learn.title: A string in memory
learn.body: `"cat"` needs 4 bytes: `c`, `a`, `t` and the terminator. `%s` prints the whole string, and `s[1]` is the single char `a`. The terminator's value is 0.

learn.title: Two kinds of quotes
learn.body: Single quotes make one character: `'a'`. Double quotes make a string: `"a"`, which holds two bytes, the letter and the terminator. They are different types and cannot be swapped.

learn.title: Length means up to the terminator
learn.body: This loop counts characters until it meets `'\0'`. It prints 3, although the array has 4 slots. This is what `strlen` does for you.

learn.title: Strings can be edited
learn.body: An array can be changed element by element: `s[1] = 'X';` turns "abc" into "aXc". Writing a terminator early cuts the string short, because everything after the first `'\0'` is ignored by `%s`.

learn.title: Size and length differ
steps: The array has 8 slots, so `sizeof s` is 8
The length is 2, the number of chars before the terminator

questions.prompt: What marks the end of a C string?
questions.explanation: Functions like `printf` and `strlen` read until they reach the terminator.

questions.prompt: How many bytes does `char s[] = "cat";` occupy? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Three letters plus the terminator make 4 bytes.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `'a'` and `"a"`?
choices: `'a'` is one char, `"a"` is a string of two bytes

questions.prompt: After `char s[] = "abc"; s[1] = 0;`, how many characters does `%s` print? Type the number.
questions.explanation: The 0 is a terminator, so the string ends after `a`.

questions.prompt: A string is an array of \_\_ ending with `'\0'`.
For `char s[8] = "hi";`, what is the string's length?
questions.explanation: The length counts chars before the terminator, not the slots.

questions.prompt: Match each item to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These four are the basics of C text.
